summary: Discovery / POC scoping for a 4-week pilot to validate latency and cost targets. Covered success criteria, QPS/concurrency expected, token distributions, and benchmark plan. Action items assigned to share logs, run Redwood baseline benchmark, and exchange security docs.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-08-30 15:00 PT | Duration: 55 minutes | Attendees: Aisha Khan (Redwood AE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Daniel Ruiz (Solstice, Head of ML), Priya Nair (Solstice, Infra), Marta Gomez (Solstice, CTO)

00:00 Aisha: Hey everybody, thanks for joining - let's do quick intros, we'll keep this scoped to POC goals and workload modeling. Jordan and I will drive technicals.
00:12 Daniel: Hey, Daniel here. Running ML platform and model infra. We're really focused on latency SLOs and predictable cost for customer-facing inference.
00:18 Priya: Priya — infra, networking and security. We'll own the VPC and peering for any pilot.
00:24 Marta: Marta, CTO. High level sponsor — want to make sure this pilot ties to the SLA ask.
00:30 Jordan: Great. Quick agenda: current stack and traffic, success criteria, QPS/concurrency and token distributions, benchmark plan and timeline.
00:40 Aisha: Quick note — we use term Redwood Dedicated vs hosted, and we can mix with hosted fallback during pilot.
00:47 Daniel: For context, we currently run an internal LLM service on prem for some features, but most customer-facing calls go to a third-party API. We're seeing cost creep and occasional spikes in latency during peak hours.
00:58 Aisha: Understood. To scope the POC we need: baseline QPS, concurrency, typical input token length, output token length, 95th/99th latency targets, and dataset for benchmarking.
01:10 Jordan: Can you share rough numbers now? Qs: QPS at peak, average concurrency per request, percentage of requests that are short vs long?
01:18 Daniel: Sure. Peak QPS is around 45 requests per second for the payments validation feature we want to move. Average QPS is 12. Concurrency — our frontend typically opens up to ~35 concurrent model requests during spikes.
01:30 Priya: Also FYI we have a bursty pattern: 09:00-11:30 and 16:00-18:00 local time, so the pilot should simulate that.
01:40 Jordan: That's helpful. Token distribution? Typical input is small: 30-70 tokens for prompts, but we do a subset of flows where user transcripts are longer — up to 800 tokens (rare, maybe 2-3% of requests). Outputs average 40-120 tokens. Does that align?
01:57 Daniel: Yes, roughly. I'd say 70% of calls are <100 input tokens, 25% between 100-300, and 5% >300. Outputs — 80% under 100, 15% 100-300, tail to 400+ very rare.
02:13 Aisha: Great. Success criteria for POC? We typically define both qualitative and quantitative: qualitative = no regressions in answer quality vs current provider; quantitative = latency SLOs, cost per 1k tokens, and error rate. Thoughts?
02:25 Marta: From exec side, we want 95th < 800ms for short calls, 99th < 1.8s for typical calls, and end-to-end p99 under 2.5s. Cost target is 30% below current provider for comparable throughput.
02:41 Jordan: Ok noted. For benchmarking we'll measure token throughput, tokens/sec, and model-level latency (init vs generation). We'll also simulate KV/prefix cache hits where applicable — you mentioned you have cached prefixes in some flows?
02:54 Daniel: Yeah, our fraud-precheck flow has repeating context — so KV cache hit rate could be 40% there. For the other flows it's low, maybe 5-10%.
03:05 Aisha: For the POC we propose: 1) Redwood runs a baseline with your sanitized traces to estimate concurrency and batching benefits, 2) 48-hour stress test that includes peak windows and long-tail requests, 3) quality evals on a 500 sample prompt set.
03:20 Daniel: That sounds reasonable. About data — how do you want logs? We can provide gzipped request logs with timestamps, anonimized user IDs and prompt hashes.
03:29 Jordan: That works. Prefer CSV with columns: timestamp, request_id, input_tokens, output_tokens_estimate, latency_observed, route (prod or beta) if available. Token histogram helps a lot.
03:41 Priya: Security questions: how long will logs be retained, and can we ingest them into a private VPC for the benchmarking? We prefer not to send any PII outside our network.
03:50 Aisha: For the initial run we can do two options: a hosted Redwood baseline where logs are uploaded to our secure S3 for benchmark, or we can run the benchmark in a Private deployment model with our infra. For pilot speed we usually start hosted with encryption at rest and delete logs after analysis. We'll send SOC2 docs and KMS integration notes.
04:08 Marta: We might need the Private option if legal can't accept outbound logs, so we want cost numbers for both.
04:15 Jordan: Noted. Technical detail — model variants and quantization: do you have a preferred family? We support standard open models and smaller quantized variants to trade-off latency/cost. Any constraints on hallucination or safety?
04:28 Daniel: Output correctness is crucial for payment flows — hallucinations could be dangerous. We'll want a model that's been validated for few-shot reliability. Latency trumps tiny accuracy gains if it affects UX.
04:38 Aisha: Understood. We'll include model recommendations and quantization profiles per workload.
04:44 Jordan: Back to traffic modeling — you said peak 45 QPS. For batching and GPU selection we need to estimate tokens/sec. Using your distribution: short requests average 60 input + 80 output = 140 tokens, mid 200 + 150 = 350, long 600 + 250 = 850. Weighted average tokens per request = approx 170-200. At 45 QPS that's ~7.6k-9k tokens/sec. Does that match your rough billing metric?
05:10 Daniel: That seems in the ballpark. Our cost math uses tokens/sec and peak concurrency to size GPU requirements. We'd be interested in Redwood's batching efficiency numbers — how much batching helps at those QPS levels.
05:24 Jordan: Right — continuous batching helps a lot for short requests. On a single A100-like worker with our runtime, you typically see good token throughput when batching windows hit ~40-60ms. We'll present microbenchmarks but the end-to-end depends on KV cache hit rate and sequence lengths.
05:40 Aisha: Proposed benchmark metrics to capture: p50/p95/p99 latencies, tokens/sec, token cost, CPU/GPU utilization, effective batching window, and failover behavior when capacity constrained. Also tie quality evals (accuracy/regression) to the same prompt set.
05:54 Priya: For the pilot we need to know network egress and whether you'll request direct VPC peering or just host endpoints behind our firewall. We prefer peering for private infra.
06:04 Jordan: We'll capture both. For Hosted baseline we'll need your firewall rule to allow outbound to Redwood ingest endpoints; for Private we can plan peering and KMS.
06:13 Aisha: Timeline — can we agree on a 4-week pilot? Week 0: data exchange and infra prep; Week 1-2: baseline runs and 48-hour stress; Week 3: quality evals and tuning; Week 4: review and decision. Is that feasible?
06:27 Marta: Yes, that's fine. Legal will want SLA draft if we move to Dedicated.
06:33 Aisha: We'll send sample SLA and pilot contract.
06:36 Daniel: Two quick technical clarifications: 1) how does Redwood handle fallback routing when Dedicated is saturated? 2) do you have per-route throttling and token caps?
06:45 Jordan: Good Qs. We support policy-based routing: route to Dedicated first, then hosted fallback to preserve availability. Per-route throttles and quotas exist; we'll show suggested settings to meet your latency SLO while controlling cost.
06:58 Priya: If we do peering, do you require any open ports or specific CIDR allowances?
07:03 Jordan: We'll provide exact CIDRs and ports (HTTPS only, 443 egress) - typical peering doesn't require open inbound ports on your side.
07:12 Aisha: Any competitors you're evaluating specifically?
07:15 Marta: We're talking to X and Y - mostly the big hyperscalers and a couple inference platform vendors. Cost and latency will decide.
07:22 Aisha: Cool. We'll include comparative notes but won't call out vendor specifics in the deck.
07:28 Daniel: Ok, last bit - success criteria checklist: 1) P99 generation latency < 1.8s for typical flows, 2) 30% cost reduction vs current provider, 3) quality parity on the 500-sample eval with <= 3% regression, 4) secure handling of logs and KMS support.
07:44 Aisha: We'll aim to design the POC to measure each of those.
07:49 Jordan: I'll prepare the benchmark config and synthetic traffic generator to emulate your peak windows and token histograms. We'll need sample traces by Friday.
07:57 Daniel: We'll work on getting logs sanitized and share token hist. Expect to upload to the secure S3 link you send.
08:05 Priya: I'll coordinate with legal on VPC/peering and confirm any compliance redlines.
08:11 Aisha: Great. Recap of next steps and owners - see action items. We'll follow up with the benchmark timeline and a calendar invite for the deep-dive next Wednesday.
08:23 Marta: Thanks everyone.
08:25 Meeting ends.

Notes / Links: Redwood POC checklist: https://redwood.ai/poc-checklist (shared), Benchmark spreadsheet (will be shared after logs), Security pack link: (sent via secure link)

Transcription notes: Automatic transcription with occasional mis-attributions and minor word errors (e.g., 'K V cache' for KV cache, 'hyperscaler X' redacted).
